chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Yusuf ibn Aqil from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a mukatab (slave who has agreed to pay a fixed sum for his freedom) who had paid part of what he was contracted to pay: that a portion of his will should be executed in proportion to what was freed from him. And he ruled regarding a mukatab who had paid half of what was upon him, and a will was made for him: that half of the will was executed. And he ruled regarding a mukatab who had paid a third of what was upon him, and a will was made for him: that a third of the will was executed.
Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr said: I copied from a book in the handwriting of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)

So-and-so, my master, died, the son of his brother, and left behind an umm walad (mother of a child) who had no child of her own. He bequeathed to her one thousand. Is the bequest valid? Does manumission apply to her? And what is her status? What is your opinion? May my soul be sacrificed for you. So he wrote (peace be upon him): 'She is manumitted from the third, and the bequest is for her.'
From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Husayn ibn Khalid al-Sayrafi, from Abu al-Hasan al-Madi (peace be upon him)

He said: I wrote to him regarding a man who died and had an umm walad, and he had given her something during his lifetime, then he died. He said: So he wrote (peace be upon him): 'For her is that which her master declared her free with during his lifetime. That is known to be for her. The testimony of a man, a woman, and a servant who are not suspected is accepted regarding that.'

key_terms.أُمُّ وَلَد: Umm walad: A slave woman who gives birth to her master's child; she becomes free upon the master's death.
key_terms.شَهَادَةُ الرَّجُلِ وَالْمَرْأَةِ: Shahadat al-rajul wa al-mar'ah: The testimony of a man and a woman, a specific evidentiary standard in fiqh.
key_terms.عِتْق: Itq: Manumission or freeing of a slave.
key_terms.مُكَاتَب: Mukatab: A slave who has entered into a contract with his master to pay a specific sum for his manumission.
key_terms.وَصِيَّة: Wasiyah: A bequest or will made by a deceased person regarding their estate.

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status and inheritance share of a mukatab and an umm walad in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the juristic principles of *kitabah* (manumission contract) and *umm walad* status, highlighting the proportional execution of bequests based on paid installments—a ruling attributed to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and rooted in the practice of Amir al-Mu'minin (AS). It further clarifies that an *umm walad* is freed from the estate's third portion and retains her specific bequest, while a master's lifetime declaration of freedom is validated by the testimony of a man, a woman, and a servant, reflecting the Shia emphasis on flexible evidentiary standards in manumission cases.
